title: Light paths and only paths in 3-connected planar graphs (Fabrici–Jendrol')
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the two theorems of Fabrici and Jendrol' (1997), for finite simple graphs with the combinatorial planarity (genus-zero rotation systems) of the registered entry Kuratowski's theorem. Theorem 1 (light_path): a 3-connected planar graph that contains a path on k ≥ 1 vertices contains such a path whose vertices all have degree at most 5k. Theorem 2 (only_paths_light): for every connected planar graph H that is not a path (not isomorphic to pathGraph on its vertex count) and every m, there is a 3-connected planar graph containing a copy of H in which every copy of H (an injective edge-preserving map) has a vertex of degree at least m. Two statements. Theorem 1 follows the proof reproduced in the Jendrol'–Voss survey (maximal counterexample, chords at major vertices, a major vertex with at most five major neighbours). Theorem 2 uses a different construction from the article's: H is completed to an edge-maximal planar graph, whose faces are triangles, and two chains of repeated stellations are inserted in every face, so that the light vertices induce disjoint paths; the result is a plane triangulation, hence 3-connected. The extremal example for 5k is not formalized.
